SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters
news.summary_raw:
AI agents often fail because their instructions, or skills, are manually modified with no guarantee of improvement. Learn how SkillOpt turns skill editing into a training process, making agent behavior more reliable without changing model weights.
The post SkillOpt: Agent skills as trainable parameters appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has announced SkillOpt, a method for turning agent skills into trainable parameters, making agent behavior more reliable. This approach eliminates the need for manual skill modifications, leading to more predictable agent performance.
news.enterprise_use: Check if your organization's robotic process automation (RPA) or AI agents use manually modified skills. If so, consider investigating alternative methods like SkillOpt to ensure reliability and efficiency in agent performance.

news.title: The ‘first’ AI-run ransomware attack still needed a human
news.summary_raw: An AI agent carried out the technical execution of a real-world ransomware attack for the first known time, but new details show a human still chose the victim, set up the infrastructure, and supplied stolen credentials — meaning it wasn't quite the fully autonomous cybercrime debut that last week's headlines suggested.
news.summary: No fully autonomous AI-run ransomware attack was performed as an AI agent only carried out the technical execution after human input. A human chose the victim, set up the infrastructure, and supplied stolen credentials.

news.title: Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity
news.summary_raw:
AI agents can't remember past conversations. They must constantly reload or retrieve context, which grows less efficient as tasks get longer and more complex. Memora solves this with a scalable memory system separating what’s stored from how it's retrieved.
The post Memora: A Harmonic Memory Representation Balancing Abstraction and Specificity appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has developed Memora, a new scalable memory system for AI agents. Memora separates what's stored from how it's retrieved, addressing the limitation of constant reloading or context retrieval.
news.enterprise_use: While this innovation doesn't directly affect your IT infrastructure, observe AI model developments and memory storage requirements as they relate to your SSO, MDM, and access management tools. This might hint at future demands for improved context handling. For now, stay informed about advancements in model scalability and adaptability.

news.title: Understanding the brain with AI-driven explanations and experiments
news.summary_raw:
Researchers introduce generative causal testing, which translates black box models into clear hypotheses and verifies them in the scanner, revealing what specific brain regions respond to in language.
The post Understanding the brain with AI-driven explanations and experiments appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has introduced generative causal testing, a method that uses AI to explain and verify complex models by translating them into clear hypotheses and testing them in brain scanners. This breakthrough helps researchers understand the brain by identifying specific regions responsible for language responses.
news.enterprise_use: This breakthrough is not directly applicable to IT engineers, but they should note advancements in AI-driven explainability and causality, which may improve the reliability of their models and tools in the future (Low signal).
